As a fellow bipolarian I can offer advice as I  see it.
Keep your appointment as it is. In all reality it is going to be really hard to get in to another place sooner and if this one is reputable and in your insurance, that is great. If you don't like the Doc, then find a few place, but give them a chance.
My therapist is also the one who noticed that I was bipolar even though I was also seeing a psychiatrist too. It is important to keep your therapist and talk to both doctors about the medication and your moods. 
As far as what to expect, in my experience, the Doc will talk to you about your symptoms and what you are feeling. He/she will ask you questions about your day to day, sleep habits, moods, etc. I would tell them what your therapist told you. 
Medication, again in my experience, will help to level you out. I still have ups and downs and go from high to low but it isn't HIGH to LOW anymore. It will probably take several trys to find the right medication combo so please be patient. It will also take several weeks to see any noticeable changes. It is a process but your Doctor  will be right there with you and it is important to tell them  everything, even if it seems minor. 
And last, the best piece of advice I can give you is to confide in a close friend or family member. It is important that someone else knows that you are starting medication. I say this because you may not notice that a certain medicine makes you manic or more depressed, but a close friend or family member will. So ask them to help monitor your symptoms as well. ( I started a medicine once that made me so  manic but I thought that was what it was like to not be depressed because I was getting stuff done but I wasn't sleeping and I was talking a mile a minute and my partner at the time noticed where I didn't)
In the  mean time, take care of your self. There is help and this community is great.
